title: Noor and the Safehouse Again
premise: Elodie Ashgrove, a disgraced intelligence analyst, receives a call on a burner phone that was decommissioned two decades ago — and hears the voice of Noor Haddad, the asset she was ordered to abandon in Tangier twenty years ago. Noor is alive, hunted by the same agency that erased her from its files, and the only way out is a dawn extraction flight that requires Elodie to surrender the one secret she has guarded all these years: proof that her own former handler orchestrated the betrayal. As hunters close in through a night of safehouses, double-crosses, and buried memories, Elodie must choose between loyalty to the institution that made them and truth to the person they never stopped loving. At the airfield at first light, Elodie trades the secret for Noor's freedom — and walks away from the flight, staying behind to face the consequences while Noor escapes with the evidence.
about_author: Silas Sterling is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent years drafting reports he was never allowed to sign his name to. He writes thrillers about people trapped between what institutions demand and what their consciences insist upon.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Twenty years after being bounced from her last agency, Elodie lives a quiet, rule-bound life in Lisbon. A burner phone she personally decommissioned in 2004 rings on her shelf. The voice on the line says only: 'Tangier. You know which door.' The beat is dread wrapped in longing.
